accepted.evidence: Dhakal p. 47 prints /cʰiulə/ “touched” as an /iu/ diphthong example; p. 73 identifies -lə as the past marker. Turner5055 gives Oriya cʰũibā and OAwadhi chuvaï “touches,” beside Nepali chunu; the Darai cʰiu- stem and past inflection fit this family.

Dhakal p. 54 prints /cʰike/ “to touch” among aspirated affricates, distinct from unaspirated /cirike/ “to split.” Turner5055 gives Nepali chunu, Maithili chūyab and Hindi chūnā “touches”; Darai cʰi- is the same touch stem.

Dhakal p. 67 repeats /cʰi.ke/ “to touch” in the attested-onset table. Turner5055 lists regional cʰu-/cʰui- touch verbs, including Oriya cʰũibā and Maithili chūyab; the independently cited token is the same Darai stem.

held.reason: Turner4996 gives Nepali chāmnu “to grope, touch, feel,” but explicitly marks the semantic link to the proposed *chambhayati as very doubtful; hold rather than attaching the doubtful head.
Dhakal p. 53 prints an aspirated retroflex in “fly.” Turner1697 §2 has regional unaspirated uḍ-/uṛ- forms, but the Darai aspiration and exact section need independent confirmation.
Turner4205 has several crossing and contaminated “weave” branches; Dhakal p. 53 /gitʰike/ lacks enough phonological detail for a precise branch.
